summary: A resident brings up what the paper says about a council vote, and the vote went the way the speaker did or did not want.
realLife: A Tempe, Arizona parks ordinance passed 7 to 0 at about 1 a.m., after 85 residents spoke against it in public comment. A Provo, Utah rezoning that neighbors opposed passed 5 to 2 after they came to the council meeting. A Laramie, Wyoming zoning ordinance passed 6 to 3 over some residents' worries about the neighborhood's character. Each was reported in the next day's local paper, which is where most neighbors learned how it came out.
sources: Phoenix New Times, Tempe passes controversial new parks ordinance: https://www.phoenixnewtimes.com/news/tempe-passes-controversial-new-parks-ordinance-backlash-22046907/

inGame: change-news (read) and your-bill-passed or failed (act or ordinance) in the bring-it-up rows: the speaker says which paper ran it and what it says about the vote on {topic}.

turns.pull: the record shows the bill passed
turns.writes: writes the paper's report that it passed, plainly

turns.pull: the record shows the bill failed
turns.writes: writes the paper's report that it fell short, with a word of sympathy
